description:
Remove the remaining restatements of declared closed vocabularies: handwritten token lists and `Debug`-rendered vocabulary values.

## Background

Each closed vocabulary (for example `State`, `Priority`, `Severity`, `GateMode`) is declared once through the `wire_vocabulary!` macro in `crates/jit/src/domain/vocabulary.rs`, which provides `ALL` and the canonical token method. Two kinds of restatement remain:

- Tests that enumerate a vocabulary's tokens by hand, e.g. the invalid-state test in `crates/jit/src/declarations/rules.rs` (around line 1831) lists all seven `State` tokens literally.
- Human output that formats vocabulary values with `{:?}`, e.g. the issue-list renderer in `crates/jit/src/output.rs` (around line 254) prints `State` and `Priority` by their Rust variant names (`InProgress`) instead of their wire tokens (`in_progress`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No code under `crates/`, test modules, integration tests and doctests included, lists the tokens of a `wire_vocabulary!`-declared vocabulary as a handwritten collection of literals; each such list derives from the vocabulary's `ALL` and its token method. Single literal values used as sample inputs are not lists and may remain.
- [hard] REQ-02: No human-facing output under `crates/` renders a `wire_vocabulary!`-declared value with `Debug` formatting; it renders the canonical wire token.
- [hard] REQ-03: JSON output data is byte-identical before and after; only description prose in the `jit --schema` document may change. Tests that asserted `Debug` names in human output assert the wire tokens instead.
title: Declared vocabularies are never restated as token lists or Debug names
